Propan-2-ol, $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHOH}$, is sometimes added to fuel to help it burn.

Fig. 3.1 shows some reactions of propan-2-ol.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Fig. 3.1

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Draw the structure of organic compound **K**.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State an observation you would make in reaction 2.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text: State the type of reaction that is shown in reaction 3.

parts.label: (a)(iv)
(b)
parts.stem:
Propan-2-ol reacts with sodium to produce $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-O}^-$ anions.

These anions react with 2-bromopropane to form compound **N**, as shown in Fig. 3.3.

{{figure:pdf_visual_03.png}}

Fig. 3.3

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction of propan-2-ol with sodium.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The reaction of 2-bromopropane with $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-O}^-$ anions follows an $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ mechanism.

Complete Fig. 3.4 to show this mechanism. Include charges, dipoles, lone pairs of electrons and curly arrows, as appropriate.

{{figure:pdf_visual_04.png}}

Fig. 3.4

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
Suggest how the rate of the $\text{S}_{\text{N}}1$ reaction would change, if at all, if 2-chloropropane were used instead of 2-bromopropane.

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
**N** is also added to petrol to make it burn more smoothly.

Construct an equation for the complete combustion of **N**, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{14}\text{O}$.
